Why we do it

It's about who they want to become.

4C is really about engaging kids in real conversation — talking with them about the things actually happening in their lives, and showing them what real life looks like. Along the way, they begin to see the goodness of God, and to ask themselves the question that shapes everything: who do I want to be?

What is 4C?

Conversations that build character.

4C Club creates a positive space where character is lived out, not just talked about — and where kids leave encouraged and connected. It's a faith-based program for 4th and 5th graders that meets once a semester, four weeks in a row, over a shared meal. Each week the kids step into a real-life story, talk about what it means, and take home one simple way to live it out.

Meet the characters

Frank & Faye lead the way.

How our time works

Every meeting, four simple beats.

1

Hear the story

Frank or Faye brings the week's true story to life.

2

Talk it out

A few questions, zero wrong answers — just real talk.

3

Make it real

One simple way to live the trait out this week.

4

Take the card

A keepsake card + memory verse to bring home.

Parents are part of it

The conversation keeps going at home.

4C isn't just the hour we're together. We equip parents to carry it home — with simple ways to talk with their kids about what we discussed, to celebrate who they've become, and to keep cheering on who they're still becoming.

Bring it home

Each week's keepsake card and memory verse are a built-in prompt to start the conversation at the dinner table.

Simple talking points

Parents get easy, no-pressure ways to ask about the week's trait and what it looked like in real life.

Growing together

Kids hear the same encouragement at club and at home — that character is something they're always still becoming.

The journey

16 traits. Four phases. Two years.

The traits build on each other — starting with how we treat the people around us and working inward toward the character that makes someone truly trustworthy.

Building Relationships Courageous Hearts Strong Character Others Can Trust
KindnessSportsmanshipInclusivityFriendship GratitudeCompassionGenerosityCourage ResponsibilityHumilityPerseveranceRespect IntegritySelf-ControlForgivenessServanthood
Bring it to your community

Want to start a 4C Club at your school or church?

4C is built to be run by parent volunteers — with a ready-to-go curriculum of stories, teaching decks, leader guides, and collectible trading cards. Wherever you are, we'd love to help you get a club started in your community.
